item.title: Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography detection of a mobile echogenic structure at the left atriotomy suture line - A case report
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Careful post-bypass TEE examination, including systematic assessment of atriotomy closure sites, may identify potentially embolic mobile echogenic structures and guide surgical management, thereby contributing to perioperative patient safety.

item.title: Patient-reported outcomes from ASCENT-03: sacituzumab govitecan vs chemotherapy in advanced triple-negative breast cancer
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: SG provided meaningful and sustained benefits in QOL vs chemotherapy. Although SG is associated with known increased gastrointestinal side effects, they can be managed and did not adversely affect functioning, long-term QOL, or treatment tolerability. These data complement previous efficacy results and support first-line SG as a new standard of care for patients with mTNBC who are not candidates for PD-(L)1 inhibitors.(ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05382299).

item.title: Artificial Intelligence in Temporomandibular Joint Imaging: Diagnostic Performance Across Input Modality-Target Pairings-A Systematic Review and Diagnostic Test Accuracy Meta-Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Sensitivity was higher when disc displacement was depicted directly on magnetic resonance imaging than when inferred from imaging that does not depict the disc. However, the cross-domain group contained only three estimates, the omnibus pairing test was not significant, and design factors were entangled. Performance should therefore be interpreted by pairing, while direct depiction versus proxy inference requires prospective testing.

item.title: Phenotypic diversity in Pierson syndrome: a case report of absent microcoria and mild renal progression
item.description: Infantile nephrotic syndrome (INS) is a heterogeneous kidney disorder characterized by proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, and edema within the first year of life. INS has a high prevalence of genetic mutations, resulting in an aggressive clinical course. Pierson syndrome manifests as congenital nephrotic syndrome, microcoria, and neurological abnormalities. However, the phenotypic spectrum is increasingly recognized as variable. We report a case of a 6-month-old female infant with INS presenting with...

item.title: Mild clinical course in siblings with NPHS1-associated familial nephrotic syndrome: two case reports
item.description: NPHS1-associated nephrotic syndrome (NS) has traditionally been considered a severe hereditary podocytopathy that presents in infancy with heavy proteinuria, poor response to immunosuppressive therapy, and early progression to kidney failure. However, accumulating evidence suggests that the clinical course varies by genotype, with some variants associated with partial preservation of nephrin function and a relatively milder phenotype. We report two brothers with NS onset beyond the congenital...

item.title: Target antigens and antigen-specific clinical phenotypes in pediatric membranous nephropathy
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence is insufficient to use antigen status alone for prognostic or treatment stratification in pediatric MN. Nevertheless, antigen typing may refine diagnosis and etiologic evaluation by prompting assessment for autoimmunity or relevant exposures. Serial anti-PLA2R measurement may support patient monitoring although tissue and serum findings are not interchangeable.

item.title: Pediatric stone disease: a urologist's perspective
item.description: Pediatric urolithiasis is increasing in prevalence worldwide and differs from adult stone disease because of its strong associations with metabolic abnormalities, genetic disorders, congenital urinary tract anomalies, and a lifelong risk of recurrence. Urologic management extends beyond stone removal to achieve durable stone-free status while preserving the developing urinary tract and minimizing cumulative treatment burden, including radiation exposure, repeated general anesthesia,...

item.title: Clinical practice recommendations for the management of Alport syndrome: a joint statement of the Korean Society of Nephrology and the Korean Society of Pediatric Nephrology
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Accordingly, these guidelines strongly recommend early RAS blockade as the cornerstone of AS, while no recommendations are made for routine use of cyclosporine, MRAs, or SGLT2i. Well-designed clinical trials are needed to expand therapeutic options and improve longterm outcomes in AS.

item.description: Identifying the factors associated with unmet medical need (UMN) is critical for designing interventional strategies. This nationwide cross- sectional study investigated the association between health literacy (HL) and UMN among Korean adults in specific age groups. Data from 5,660 adults who participated in the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (2023), along with available data on HL and UMN, were analysed. The primary obstacle lies in integrating zero-energy, efficient cooling solutions without compromising comfort. As urbanization intensifies, innovative solutions must balance environmental impact with functionality. item.description: Communication with the lymphoid microenvironment is essential for the survival and proliferation of neoplastic B cells in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). item.title: Endothelial IFI16 drives vasculopathy and profibrotic remodeling in systemic sclerosis by activating JAK/STAT signaling
item.description: CONCLUSION: Collectively, endothelial IFI16 coupled IFN-I signaling to vasculopathy and fibrotic remodeling via JAK-STAT activation, highlighting IFI16 as a promising therapeutic target in SSc vasculopathy and the subsequent fibrosis.

item.title: A Comprehensive Radiomics Model for Predicting Progression-Free Survival in High-Risk Neuroblastoma Based on CT Imaging
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study validates a PFS predictive model combining clinical, CT, and radiomic features, providing a robust tool for individualized prognosis in high-risk NB patients.

item.title: Contribution of risk factors to racial/ethnic disparities in tuberculosis among US-born persons
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Eliminating racial/ethnic disparities in TB will require more than addressing individual risk factors. Combatting structural or community-level determinants of TB, including treating infection to prevent disease, will be important for accelerating TB elimination.

item.title: Modulation of the teleost gut-microbiome-immunity axis in Nile tilapia Oreochromis niloticus following intestinal delivery of a microencapsulated deep-sea Lactococcus lactis strain
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Integrative analysis suggests that L. lactis L25_4 facilitates a physiological trade-off, where a reinforced physical mucosal barrier allows the freshwater host to downregulate energetically expensive immune responses in favor of reduced inflammatory gene expression. Encapsulated deep-sea bacterium can trigger cross-ecosystem homeostatic recalibration, providing a robust framework for microbiota-driven modulation along the vertebrate gut-microbiome-immunity axis.

item.title: Cost-utility analysis of surgical revascularization versus conservative management for adult moyamoya disease patients with posterior hemorrhage in Japan
item.description: CONCLUSION: Surgical revascularization is likely to be cost-effective for adult MMD patients with posterior hemorrhage within the Japanese healthcare system, although limited evidence leaves uncertainty about long-term rebleeding risks and the durability of surgical benefit.

item.description: CONCLUSION: SSK2 c.793A>G is closely associated with AmB resistance and functionally contributes to the resistance phenotype. SSK2 could serve as a potential therapeutic target for developing AmB synergistic sensitizers and as a research direction for future synergistic treatments of clinically resistant C. gattii strains.

item.description: CONCLUSION: This comprehensive genome analysis of Nocardia, representing the most complete sampling to date, clarifies phylogeny, reclassifies misassigned strains, identifies potential novel species, and reveals clade-specific patterns of virulence, resistance, and secondary metabolism.

By introducing actionable Tier-3 indicators, the framework operationalizes the assessment of broader vaccine benefits and offers a practical tool to support equitable and comprehensive evidence-based policymaking. item.title: Estimating Risk of Measles Virus Transmission in Countries with Measles Elimination Status: A Comparative Measles Seroprevalence Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Achieving measles elimination does not guarantee that population-level protection will be sustained. Despite high overall seroprevalence, important immunity gaps persist among infants and young children, and some countries do not maintain the required herd immunity threshold following elimination. Targeted interventions are needed to close immunity gaps and strengthen national population immunity to prevent measles resurgence.

item.title: Evidence-based policy improvements for lipid lowering therapy: a focus on reducing clinical inertia and improving cardiovascular outcomes
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Despite substantial evidence linking low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) reduction to improved cardiovascular outcomes, a significant implementation gap persists. Clinical inertia, defined as failure to initiate or intensify therapy despite suboptimal control, remains a key barrier to achieving guideline-recommended LDL-C goals, particularly in high-risk populations.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Open disc repositioning with anchoring was associated with greater bite-force recovery and more symmetric superficial jaw-elevator activation during clenching. The age-stratified findings showed a potentially clinically relevant pattern favouring surgery, particularly among patients aged ≤ 30 years. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation and do not establish an age-specific treatment threshold.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Our study provides novel insights into DLBCL pathogenesis by suggesting that the CCL21/CCR7 axis contributes to tumor aggressiveness at least partly through activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, leading to mesenchymal-like phenotypic remodeling. These findings support CCR7 as a potential therapeutic target and suggest that antibody-mediated CCR7 blockade warrants further in vivo validation.

item.title: Beyond AI readiness: an information-integrity readiness framework for governing synthetic media in Somalia
item.description: Generative artificial intelligence has transformed synthetic media from a specialized technical concern into a systemic governance challenge. Existing AI readiness frameworks evaluate whether states can adopt, deploy, and regulate AI, but they do not systematically assess whether societies can preserve the authenticity, trustworthiness, and resilience of information circulating within AI-enabled environments. item.title: Peripheral microvascular function and in-stent late lumen loss after percutaneous coronary intervention: a retrospective cohort study with an exploratory analysis by implanted stent diameter
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Peripheral microvascular endothelial function measured by the reactive hyperemia index (RHI) with EndoPAT predicts cardiovascular outcomes, and post-procedural RHI has been associated with binary in-stent restenosis. Whether pre-procedural RHI relates to in-stent late lumen loss (LLL) measured by quantitative coronary angiography (QCA) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and whether any association depends on device caliber, has not been established.

item.title: Association of Cholinesterase Inhibitor-Memantine Combination Therapy With Long-Term Community Management and Mortality in Patients With Dementia: A Nationwide Retrospective Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: AChEI-memantine combination therapy was associated with more favorable 5-year outcomes than memantine monotherapy among later memantine initiators. These observational findings require confirmation with analyses addressing clinical severity, treatment selection, and time-related bias.

item.title: Mediation of the Association Between APOE Genotype and Cognitive Change Through Alzheimer's Disease Biomarkers in Patients With Mild Cognitive Impairment
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Lower CSF Aβ42 showed a significant statistical indirect association between APOE ε4 carrier status and 36-month clinical worsening in MCI. These observational findings do not establish a causal mediating mechanism.

item.title: Low Diastolic Blood Pressure and Cardiometabolic Burden Predict Heart Failure in Treated Hypertensive Patients: Insights From the Korean Hypertension Cohort
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Hypertensive patients had a markedly higher long-term incidence of HF. Beyond BP levels, metabolic syndrome and albuminuria were independent determinants of HF development, highlighting the importance of comprehensive cardiometabolic and renal risk assessment in hypertensive patients.
